findings.finding: ATW's senior secured convertible notes (about $90M of facilities, 7%, fixed conversion prices of $11.50-$30 against a $4.31 spot) convert in practice only at market-linked prices: 93% of the lowest 8-day VWAP on installments, with up to four installments accelerable per period. That makes the holder a continuous, price-insensitive seller of registered resale shares on any trading day, including 2026-10-13.
findings.mechanism_in_window: Note section 8(e) lets the holder accelerate installment conversions on any trading day within the installment period, and the conversion shares are already registered for resale (424B4, 2026-07-15). The supply therefore can land on 2026-10-13 without a new filing. It is not dated to that day, which is why it is sized small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock is down 75.5% over 60 sessions and sits at a 52-week position of 0.003, with 4 of its 5 comparable falls followed by a lower close (baseline). That is consistent with persistent supply but not attributable to it from a document.
findings.why_not_priced: The price has taken today's selling but not the next round of conversions, which are discounted to the trailing low VWAP and so rise in share count as the price falls. If it held this, the stock would trade at a discount to peers' bounce days. That cannot be observed, so the finding is small.
